reason: [q038] The answer counts units set out in approved business plans ('the number of units to be constructed'), not dwellings built, under construction, contracted or handed over. The breakdown key sector= isn't among the keys the data model defines, and the indicator says to use category= for site or stage. The Dominica rows put stage in category= (e.g. bellevue_chopin_under_construction). So the breakdown becomes category=social_housing_approved_in_business_plans, which names the stage and keeps these rows apart from built or contracted counts. No better existing indicator: cbi_projects_approved counts projects, not dwellings, and cbi_project_hotel_rooms is for hotel rooms. If the second reader thinks 'approved, planned' is outside cbi_funded_housing_units altogether, a planned-units indicator would have to be proposed (decision 11). Values, period and notes are right and stay. Possible side issue, not changed here: 2017 and 2018 are closed years given in an official answer, but the status is 'provisional'. | Evidence: irl-oir-wa-2019-11-06, Written answer 6 Nov 2019, Questions 86, 87 and 94 [45716/19, 45717/19, 45715/19], Minister for Justice and Equality: "It is a requirement under the Immigrant Investor Programme (IIP) that applicants submit detailed business plans. The Plans for Investment projects involving construction set out, in detail, the number of units to be constructed. In 2017, 5 nursing home projects and 566 social housing units were approved. In 2018, 4 nursing homes and 884 social housing units were approved. In 2019, 5 nursing homes and some 560 social housing units were approved." | Second reader (irl-oir-wa-2019-11-06, written answer 6 Nov 2019, Qs 86, 87, 94 (stored XML)): "The Plans for Investment projects involving construction set out, in detail, the number of units to be constructed. In 2017, 5 nursing home projects and 566 social housing units were approved. In 2018, 4 nursing homes and 884 social housing units were approved. In 2019, 5 nursing homes and some 560 social housing units were approved." Units are 'approved' in business plans, not built or under construction, so the new category label social_housing_approved_in_business_plans is accurate, and the indicator definition says breakdown category= for site or stage (sector= was off-convention). Caveat: the change leaves the rows in cbi_funded_housing_units (defined as dwellings built, under construction, contracted or handed over), so anyone summing that indicator across categories could still add planned units to built ones; a move to an approved/planned indicator (e.g. cbi_projects_approved) would be cleaner, but the proposed edit is correct as far as it goes.

value: Naturalisation by Prime Minister's decree on the recommendation of a Cabinet unit (members from Foreign Affairs, Interior, Investment/International Cooperation and security agencies), under Art. 4 bis of the Nationality Law as replaced by Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019). Routes and amounts set by PM Decree 3099/2019 (Dec 2019; text not obtained), amended by PM Decrees 876/2023 (in force 3 Mar 2023) and 3562/2023 (19 Sep 2023); the unit was organised by PM Decree 647/2020. Current routes: property USD 300,000; investment project USD 350,000 plus USD 100,000 to the Treasury; USD 500,000 deposit at the Central Bank refunded in EGP after 3 years without interest; USD 250,000 non-refundable payment. USD 10,000 application fee. Selling the property or project within 5 years requires a USD 250,000 payment to keep citizenship. No residence requirement. Each grant is published as a named PM decree in the Official Gazette; no aggregate statistics are published. 'launched' is Law 140/2019 (30 Jul 2019), the first text making investment a route (decision 14); amounts were set by the December 2019 decree and applications reportedly opened in 2020.
